questions.questionText: Using the data in Extract D (Figure 3), calculate the median number of storm overflow hours by water company in 2022.

A government announces that, over a 10 year period, it plans to reduce the number of tradable pollution permits it issues each year. Which one of the following is the most likely response from firms in industries affected by the announcement?
options: Firms are likely to delay investment into more environmentally friendly production methods
Only the firms that generate the most pollution are likely to react at all
Over time, more firms will have an incentive to reduce their pollution
The firms with the lowest costs of reducing pollution will buy the most permits

questions.questionText: Extract C (lines 3–4) states that ‘the mining, manufacturing and disposal process for batteries could soon become an environmental disaster.’ With the help of a diagram, explain why the production and sale of lithium-ion batteries might lead to market failure.

Extract B (lines 20–21) states that ‘all vehicle owners should be forced to pay the full costs of their driving. This would incentivise people to consider using public transport, cycling or walking.’ Evaluate policies that could be used to reduce the environmental impact of all types of car.

Figure 5 shows the marginal private and social benefit (MPB and MSB) curves and the marginal private and social cost (MPC and MSC) curves for a product. The socially optimal level of output for this product is
options: 2 units
3 units
4 units
5 units

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a reason why the extension of property rights is likely to reduce market failure?
options: Merit goods will no longer be underconsumed in a free market.
Producers will be more likely to have to pay compensation for pollution.
Public goods will no longer be subject to the free-rider problem.
The inequality in the distribution of income and wealth will be reduced.

questions.questionText: Figure 1 shows the marginal private benefit and marginal social benefit (MPB and MSB) curves and the marginal private cost and marginal social cost (MPC and MSC) curves in the market for a good. The diagram represents a good with
options: negative externalities in production and consumption.
negative externalities in production and positive externalities in consumption.
positive externalities in production and consumption.
positive externalities in production and negative externalities in consumption.

questions.questionText: The UK government has set a target to reduce net greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions to zero by 2050. To what extent, if at all, do the data suggest that to achieve its net-zero emissions target, the government should focus on reducing GHG emissions from the transport sector? You must use the data in Extract C to support your assessment.
Explain why, without government intervention, markets are likely to allocate too few resources to dealing with the problem of climate change.

Using the data in Extract A (Figure 1) calculate the percentage of all plastics produced in the period 1950–2015 which have either been sent to landfill or incinerated. Give your answer to one decimal place.
Explain how the data in Extract A (Figure 2) show that higher living standards lead to greater volumes of waste per capita being produced.

Extract C (lines 17–19) states: ‘Many environmental economists suggest that making firms pay for the costs of landfill associated with their products, or taxing raw material inputs, will be necessary to ensure a sustainable future for all.’ Using the extracts and your knowledge of economics, evaluate policies, if any, that governments in developed countries should pursue to reduce waste and encourage the recycling of waste products.

Figure 6 shows the marginal private and social benefit (MPB and MSB) curves and the marginal private and social cost (MPC and MSC) curves in the market for domestically produced solar panels. The initial market equilibrium is at E1. To correct the market failure, the government introduces a subsidy to domestic manufacturers of solar panels of £200 per unit produced. Which one of the following represents the total amount of subsidy payments made by the government in the first year of the scheme?
options: £20 million.
£25 million.
£75 million.
£100 million.

questions.questionText: The existence of negative externalities in consumption results in a misallocation of resources. This is because at the free market level of output the
options: marginal private benefit is greater than the marginal private cost.
marginal private cost is greater than the marginal social cost.
marginal social benefit is less than the marginal social cost.
marginal social cost is less than the marginal private benefit.

questions.questionText: Explain why the use of petrol and diesel cars may be a source of market failure.
Assess the view that regulation is a better policy for dealing with the problem of air pollution than the allocation of property rights or taxation.
To what extent, if at all, do the data suggest that the reliance on fossil fuels to produce energy is falling? You must use the data in Extract C to support your assessment.
Explain why, in a free market, sugary drinks may be overconsumed.

The diagram below shows the marginal private and social benefit (MPB and MSB) curves and the marginal private and social cost (MPC and MSC) curves in a market where there are positive externalities in production. At the free market equilibrium, market failure occurs. Which one of the following is correct?
options: As a result of this market failure, consumer surplus is reduced by ZXY
As a result of this market failure, there is a deadweight loss to society of P3P1XZ
P1 minus P3 is the subsidy per unit that is required to correct the market failure and achieve the social optimum
The diagonal distance XY shows the amount by which marginal private cost exceeds marginal social cost at OQ2
